sentence: The car broke down on the way to the airport
hint: Past tense of 'break down' is 'broke down'
explanation: 'Break down' significa dejar de funcionar. Pasado: 'broke down' (irregular). 'Breaked' no existe.

sentence: They had to call off the meeting because of the storm
explanation: 'Call off' significa cancelar. 'Had to' expresa obligación en pasado. Es separable: 'call the meeting off' también es correcto.

sentence: She came across an old photograph while cleaning the attic
explanation: 'Come across' significa encontrar algo por casualidad. Pasado: 'came across'. 'While' + gerundio para acciones simultáneas.

sentence: You should cut down on sugar if you want to lose weight
explanation: 'Cut down on' significa reducir el consumo. 'Should' va seguido de la forma base del verbo.

sentence: I need to figure out how to solve this problem
explanation: 'Figure out' significa entender o resolver. 'How to' introduce el método.

sentence: He hung up the phone without saying goodbye
hint: Past tense of 'hang up' is 'hung up'
explanation: 'Hang up' significa colgar el teléfono. Pasado: 'hung up'. Es separable: 'hung the phone up' también es correcto.

sentence: We are looking forward to meeting you next week
hint: 'Look forward to' is followed by a gerund
explanation: 'Look forward to' significa esperar algo con ilusión. Aquí 'to' es una preposición, así que va seguido de un gerundio.

sentence: The teacher told the students to hand in their essays
explanation: 'Hand in' significa entregar. Es separable: 'hand their essays in' también es correcto.

sentence: She has been putting off the decision for months
explanation: 'Put off' significa posponer. Es separable: 'putting the decision off' también es correcto.

sentence: They set up a new company in London last year
explanation: 'Set up' significa establecer o montar. Pasado: 'set up' (misma forma). Es separable: 'set a new company up' también es correcto.

sentence: It took her months to get over the flu
hint: Subject + verb + infinitive + phrasal verb + object
explanation: 'Get over' significa recuperarse de una enfermedad o de una experiencia difícil.

sentence: We ran out of milk this morning
hint: Subject + phrasal verb + object + time expression
explanation: 'Run out of' significa quedarse sin algo.

sentence: The police are looking into the missing car
explanation: 'Look into' significa investigar algo.

sentence: She takes after her mother in many ways
hint: Subject + phrasal verb + object + prepositional phrase
explanation: 'Take after' significa parecerse a un familiar en aspecto o carácter.

sentence: He decided to go through with the plan despite the risks
hint: Subject + verb + infinitive + phrasal verb + object
explanation: 'Go through with' significa completar una acción aunque sea difícil o arriesgada.

sentence: The team carried out a detailed investigation
explanation: 'Carry out' significa realizar o llevar a cabo. Es separable pero suele usarse junto.

sentence: We need to deal with this problem immediately
hint: Subject + verb + infinitive + phrasal verb + object
explanation: 'Deal with' significa ocuparse de algo. No es separable.

sentence: You can always count on your best friend
hint: Subject + modal + adverb + phrasal verb + object
explanation: 'Count on' significa confiar en alguien. No es separable.

sentence: He finally gave in to their demands
explanation: 'Give in' significa ceder o rendirse. No es separable.

sentence: Young players look up to famous athletes
explanation: 'Look up to' significa admirar a alguien. No es separable.
